newsitem.title: INDIA: India ONGC to get higher price for crude.
newsitem.headline: India ONGC to get higher price for crude.

text.p: The state-run Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC) and Oil India Ltd (OIL) would get marginal relief following the government's decision to raise prices of indigenous crude, oil analysts said on Thursday.
A cabinet panel of the federal government on Wednesday approved a proposal to revise crude oil price paid to ONGC and OIL to 1,991 rupees per tonne from 1,741 rupees.

It also asked crude oil producers to pay higher royalty of 578 rupees per tonne of oil to Indian states (up from 528 rupees) for oil produced onshore and to the federal government for oil produced from offshore fields.
The revised price is effective April 1, 1996, according to newspaper reports.
Crude oil price paid to ONGC and OIL was last revised in 1993/94 (April-March).
Even after the revision, the price paid to ONGC and OIL works out to about $13.0 per barrel compared to the global price of $24.0, analysts said.
"It is not enough to help them achieve the 15 percent return on capital (stipulated under the administered pricing mechanism)," an oil analyst said.

The government may not implement the hike immediately in view of the mounting oil pool account deficit which the petroleum ministry estimates at 200 billion rupees for 1996/97 (April-March), oil analysts said.
But both ONGC and OIL will have to pay higher royalty with immediate effect, analysts said.
ONGC accounts for almost 90 percent of India's oil and gas production.
